symbols.name: vector space
symbols.meaning: A vector space over the field $F$ of scalars, on which the bilinear form is defined.
symbols.quote: Let $E$ be a vector space over the field $F$ of scalars.

symbols.name: vector
symbols.quote: The letters $\xi$ and $\eta$ denote vectors of $E$ here, not the ring elements of earlier pages.

symbols.name: vector
symbols.quote: The letters $\xi$ and $\eta$ denote vectors of $E$ here, not the ring elements of earlier pages.

symbols.name: subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of $E$, whose orthogonal complement is taken.

symbols.name: orthogonal complement
symbols.meaning: The set of vectors of $E$ orthogonal to every vector of $U$.
symbols.quote: Its orthogonal complement $U^\perp$ is the set of vectors $\xi$ in $E$ with $\langle \xi,\eta\rangle=0$ for every $\eta$ in $U$.

symbols.name: first coordinate
symbols.meaning: The first coordinate of the vector $\xi$ in $\mathbb{Q}^2$.
symbols.quote: For example, let $E=\mathbb{Q}^2$, and write $\xi_1$ and $\xi_2$ for the first and second coordinates of $\xi$, and $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ for those of $\eta$.

symbols.name: second coordinate
symbols.meaning: The second coordinate of the vector $\xi$ in $\mathbb{Q}^2$.
symbols.quote: For example, let $E=\mathbb{Q}^2$, and write $\xi_1$ and $\xi_2$ for the first and second coordinates of $\xi$, and $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ for those of $\eta$.

symbols.name: first coordinate
symbols.meaning: The first coordinate of the vector $\eta$ in $\mathbb{Q}^2$.
symbols.quote: For example, let $E=\mathbb{Q}^2$, and write $\xi_1$ and $\xi_2$ for the first and second coordinates of $\xi$, and $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ for those of $\eta$.

symbols.name: second coordinate
symbols.meaning: The second coordinate of the vector $\eta$ in $\mathbb{Q}^2$.
symbols.quote: For example, let $E=\mathbb{Q}^2$, and write $\xi_1$ and $\xi_2$ for the first and second coordinates of $\xi$, and $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ for those of $\eta$.

symbols.name: basis vector
symbols.meaning: The $i$-th vector of the fixed basis of $E$.
symbols.quote: Fix a basis $e_1,\dots,e_m$ of $E$, where $m$ is the dimension of $E$, and write $e_i$ for its $i$-th vector.

symbols.name: form matrix
symbols.meaning: The $m\times m$ matrix of the form in the chosen basis.
symbols.quote: Let $A$ be the $m\times m$ matrix with entries $A_{ij}=\langle e_i,e_j\rangle$, so that $\langle \xi,\eta\rangle=\xi^{\mathsf T}A\eta$.

symbols.name: transpose
symbols.meaning: The operation turning a column of coordinates into the row with the same entries.
symbols.quote: Here $\xi^{\mathsf T}$ is the transpose of $\xi$, the row of its coordinates.

symbols.name: all-one matrix
symbols.meaning: The $h\times h$ matrix whose entries are all $1$.
symbols.quote: Let $J$ be the all-one $h\times h$ matrix.

symbols.name: all-one vector
symbols.quote: Since $J=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}$, where $\mathbf 1$ is the column of $h$ ones, $J$ has [eigenvalues](eigenvalue.md) $h$ on $\mathbf 1$ and $0$ on vectors whose coordinates sum to $0$.

symbols.name: second triple
symbols.meaning: A second triple, another three-element subset of $[h]$.
symbols.quote: For another triple $T'$, $t_T^{\mathsf T}t_{T'}=|T\cap T'|$, the shared count, and $t_T^{\mathsf T}Jt_{T'}=3\cdot 3=9$.

relations.quote: A bilinear form on $E$ is a special case of a [bilinear map](bilinear-map.md): it takes two vectors $\xi$ and $\eta$ of $E$ and returns the scalar $\langle \xi,\eta\rangle$ in $F$, linear in each argument when the other is fixed.
The form is written with the matrices of [linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).
Hence $A$ has eigenvalues $1-h/9=-91/9$ and $1$, and nondegeneracy is decided by the [eigenvalues](eigenvalue.md) of $A$: neither is zero.
The form below is the setting for the paper's [bit network](bit-network.md).
